observed_structure: Two threadgroup arrays retain one maximum and one exponential-denominator partial per SIMDgroup.
Each thread starts with a finite-minimum maximum reference and a zero denominator, then loads N_READS values per loop iteration with out-of-range tail slots set to Limits<AccT>::min.
After each chunk maximum update, the prior denominator is rescaled by softmax_exp(old_max-new_max) before exponentials relative to the new maximum are added.
A SIMDgroup merge first selects a common maximum, aligns each lane denominator to it, and sums the aligned denominators.
Lane zero publishes each SIMDgroup maximum before a threadgroup barrier; the group denominators are then aligned to the merged maximum, published, synchronized, and summed.
After taking the reciprocal denominator, the kernel re-reads the input and writes softmax_exp(input-global_max) times that reciprocal with a guarded tail.
variant_notes: N_READS batches multiple scores into one maximum update rather than applying a scalar recurrence once per score.
Out-of-range chunk slots use Limits<AccT>::min, and the cited span introduces no separate NaN or infinity repair branch.

Besides the maximum reference, the online summary carries only the exponential denominator; output probabilities are regenerated by a final input pass rather than by carrying a value-weighted payload.
